questions.question: What is the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape?
questions.explanation: The Event Horizon is the threshold where gravitational pull becomes infinite and escape velocity exceeds the speed of light.
questions.funFact: If you fell into a stellar-mass black hole, gravitational stretching would turn you into cosmic spaghetti ('Spaghettification')!

questions.question: How long does light from the Sun take to travel across space and reach Earth?
questions.explanation: Traveling at 300,000 km/s across 149.6 million km, sunlight takes roughly 8 minutes and 20 seconds to reach our eyes.
questions.funFact: If the Sun vanished right this second, Earth would stay lit and in orbit for another 8 minutes and 20 seconds!

questions.question: Which is the largest planet in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is more than twice as massive as all the other planets combined.
questions.funFact: More than 1,300 Earths could fit inside Jupiter.

questions.question: Which planet is the hottest in our Solar System?
questions.explanation: Venus's thick carbon dioxide atmosphere causes a runaway greenhouse effect, with surface temperatures around 465 degrees C, hotter than Mercury.
questions.funFact: Venus is hot enough to melt lead.

questions.question: Which planet has a day longer than its year?
questions.explanation: Venus takes about 243 Earth days to rotate once but only about 225 days to orbit the Sun.
questions.funFact: Venus also spins backwards compared to most planets, so the Sun rises in the west.

questions.question: Which pair of planets is thought to have 'diamond rain' deep inside?
questions.explanation: Extreme pressure and heat inside Uranus and Neptune are believed to squeeze carbon into diamonds that sink through the interior.
questions.funFact: Experiments with lasers have recreated this process in the lab.

questions.question: Olympus Mons on Mars is the tallest known volcano in the Solar System. About how tall is it?
questions.explanation: Olympus Mons stands about 22 km high, roughly two and a half times the height of Mount Everest.
questions.funFact: It is so wide that if you stood on it you couldn't see its edges because of the planet's curvature.

questions.question: What percentage of the Solar System's total mass is in the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun holds roughly 99.86% of all mass in the Solar System, leaving very little for all the planets combined.
questions.funFact: Jupiter makes up most of the remaining mass.

questions.question: What does a teaspoon of neutron star material weigh?
questions.explanation: Neutron stars are so dense that a teaspoon of their material would weigh billions of tonnes on Earth.
questions.funFact: A neutron star is only about 20 km wide but has more mass than the Sun.

questions.question: What is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun?
questions.explanation: Proxima Centauri is about 4.24 light-years away and is a small red dwarf.
questions.funFact: With today's fastest spacecraft, the trip would take tens of thousands of years.

questions.question: Which large galaxy is on course to collide with the Milky Way in billions of years?
questions.explanation: Andromeda is about 2.5 million light-years away and approaching us, with a merger expected in about 4 to 5 billion years.
questions.funFact: Even in a galaxy collision, individual stars will almost never crash into each other.

questions.question: About how old is the universe?
questions.explanation: Measurements of the cosmic microwave background put the age of the universe at about 13.8 billion years.
questions.funFact: Earth is only about 4.5 billion years old.

questions.question: Who accidentally discovered the cosmic microwave background radiation in 1965?
questions.explanation: Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson detected a persistent radio noise that turned out to be the afterglow of the Big Bang.
questions.funFact: They first thought the noise came from pigeon droppings on their antenna.

questions.question: About what percentage of the universe is ordinary matter (stars, planets, us)?
questions.explanation: Ordinary matter is about 5% of the universe, with about 27% dark matter and 68% dark energy.
questions.funFact: Scientists still don't know what dark matter and dark energy are.

questions.question: Who was the first human to travel into space?
questions.explanation: Soviet cosmonaut Yuri Gagarin orbited Earth on 12 April 1961 aboard Vostok 1.
questions.funFact: His flight lasted only 108 minutes.

questions.question: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969 during Apollo 11.
questions.funFact: Michael Collins stayed in orbit and never walked on the Moon.

questions.question: How many humans have walked on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon across six Apollo landings between 1969 and 1972.
questions.funFact: No human has been back on the Moon since 1972.

questions.question: Which spacecraft launched in 1977 became the first to enter interstellar space?
questions.explanation: Voyager 1 crossed the heliopause into interstellar space in 2012 and is the most distant human-made object.
questions.funFact: Each Voyager carries a golden record with sounds and images from Earth.

questions.question: The famous 'Pale Blue Dot' photograph of Earth was taken by which spacecraft?
questions.explanation: Voyager 1 took the image in 1990 from about 6 billion km away, at the request of Carl Sagan.
questions.funFact: In it, Earth appears as less than a single pixel.

questions.question: On which date did the James Webb Space Telescope launch?
questions.explanation: JWST launched on Christmas Day 2021 aboard an Ariane 5 rocket and observes mainly in infrared light.
questions.funFact: It sits about 1.5 million km from Earth at the L2 point.

questions.question: Chandrayaan-3 made history in 2023 by landing near which part of the Moon?
questions.explanation: On 23 August 2023, India became the first country to soft-land near the Moon's south pole.
questions.funFact: India also became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon.

questions.question: India's Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission) made India the first country to do what?
options: Reach Mars orbit on its first attempt
questions.explanation: Mangalyaan entered Mars orbit in September 2014 on ISRO's first try, at a cost lower than many Hollywood films.
questions.funFact: The mission cost about 450 crore rupees.

questions.question: ISRO's Aditya-L1 mission, launched in 2023, was sent to study what?
questions.explanation: Aditya-L1 is India's first space-based solar observatory, positioned near the Sun-Earth L1 point.
questions.funFact: L1 lets it watch the Sun continuously without eclipses.

questions.question: Which planet is less dense than water and would theoretically float?
questions.explanation: Saturn's average density is about 0.69 g/cm3, lower than water's 1 g/cm3.
questions.funFact: You would need a bathtub bigger than the planet to try it.

questions.question: Which planet rotates on its side, tilted at about 98 degrees?
questions.explanation: Uranus's extreme tilt is thought to come from an ancient massive collision, so it rolls around the Sun like a ball.
questions.funFact: Its poles get about 42 years of continuous sunlight followed by 42 years of darkness.

questions.question: Jupiter's Great Red Spot is what?
options: A giant storm larger than Earth
questions.explanation: The Great Red Spot is an enormous anticyclonic storm that has been observed for well over a century and is wider than Earth.
questions.funFact: It has been shrinking in recent decades.

questions.question: In 2006, Pluto was reclassified as what?
questions.explanation: The International Astronomical Union defined 'planet' in 2006, and Pluto didn't meet the requirement of clearing its orbit.
questions.funFact: Pluto is smaller than Earth's Moon.

questions.question: Which moon of Jupiter is believed to hide a huge subsurface ocean beneath its ice?
questions.explanation: Europa's icy shell is thought to cover a global salty ocean, making it a prime target in the search for alien life.
questions.funFact: It may hold about twice as much water as all of Earth's oceans.

questions.question: Which moon in our Solar System has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane?
questions.explanation: Saturn's moon Titan has a dense nitrogen atmosphere and hydrocarbon lakes and seas on its surface.
questions.funFact: NASA's Dragonfly mission is planned to fly a rotorcraft there.

questions.question: Why can't you hear sound in space?
options: There is no medium (air) for sound waves to travel through
questions.explanation: Sound needs a medium like air to travel, and space is a near-vacuum.
questions.funFact: Astronauts talk to each other on radios, which use electromagnetic waves, not sound.

questions.question: What happens to astronauts' height in space?
questions.explanation: Without gravity compressing the spine, astronauts can grow up to a couple of inches (about 5 cm) taller.
questions.funFact: They return to normal height soon after coming back to Earth.

questions.question: What is the most abundant element in the universe?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen makes up roughly 75% of the ordinary matter in the universe.
questions.funFact: Most of the hydrogen in your body was created in the Big Bang.

questions.question: About how fast does the ground move due to Earth's rotation at the equator?
questions.explanation: Earth rotates once every 24 hours, giving a speed at the equator of roughly 1,670 km/h.
questions.funFact: Earth is also orbiting the Sun at about 107,000 km/h.

questions.question: A bolt of lightning is about how much hotter than the Sun's surface?
questions.explanation: Lightning heats air to around 30,000 K, about five times hotter than the Sun's roughly 5,500 degrees C surface.
questions.funFact: A lightning bolt lasts only a fraction of a second.

questions.question: What food is often said to never spoil due to its low moisture and natural acidity?
questions.explanation: Honey's low water content and acidity make it extremely resistant to bacteria, and edible honey has been found in ancient Egyptian tombs.
questions.funFact: Bees fan honey with their wings to reduce moisture.

questions.question: Why are bananas slightly radioactive?
options: They are grown near nuclear plants
questions.explanation: Bananas are rich in potassium, a small fraction of which is the radioactive isotope potassium-40.
questions.funFact: The radiation is so small it's harmless; it's even used as an informal 'banana equivalent dose' unit.

questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explanation: An octopus has two branchial hearts for the gills and one systemic heart for the body.
questions.funFact: Octopus blood is blue because it uses copper-based haemocyanin.

questions.question: Roughly how much of our DNA do humans share with chimpanzees?
questions.explanation: Humans and chimpanzees share about 98 to 99% of their DNA, showing a recent common ancestor.
questions.funFact: We also share about half our genes with a banana.

questions.question: What is absolute zero, the lowest possible temperature?
questions.explanation: Absolute zero is 0 Kelvin, or -273.15 degrees C, where particles have minimal thermal motion.
questions.funFact: Scientists have cooled atoms to within a tiny fraction of a degree above it.

questions.question: At what temperature is water at its densest?
questions.explanation: Water is densest at about 4 degrees C, so ice floats and lakes freeze from the top down.
questions.funFact: This odd property allows aquatic life to survive winter.

questions.question: Why do GPS satellites have to account for Einstein's theory of relativity?
options: Their clocks tick at different rates than clocks on Earth
questions.explanation: Satellite clocks run differently due to their speed and weaker gravity, and without correction GPS would drift by kilometres a day.
questions.funFact: The net effect is about 38 microseconds per day.

questions.question: Schrodinger's cat is a famous thought experiment about which idea in physics?
questions.explanation: The cat is described as both alive and dead until observed, illustrating superposition in quantum mechanics.
questions.funFact: Schrodinger proposed it to show how strange he thought the idea was.

questions.question: The Chandrasekhar limit, about 1.4 solar masses, decides the fate of what?
questions.explanation: Subrahmanyan Chandrasekhar showed that a white dwarf above about 1.4 solar masses collapses, leading to a supernova or neutron star.
questions.funFact: He won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1983.

questions.question: Which Indian scientist won the 1930 Nobel Prize in Physics for the scattering of light?
questions.explanation: C. V. Raman discovered the Raman effect, and India celebrates National Science Day on 28 February to mark it.
questions.funFact: He was the first Asian to win a Nobel Prize in science.

questions.question: About how hot is the core of the Sun?
questions.explanation: The Sun's core is around 15 million degrees C, hot enough for hydrogen fusion.
questions.funFact: The Sun's surface is much cooler than its outer atmosphere, the corona.

questions.question: What will the Sun eventually become in about 5 billion years?
questions.explanation: The Sun will swell into a red giant, likely engulfing Mercury and Venus, then shed layers and become a white dwarf.
questions.funFact: It is currently about halfway through its life.

questions.question: Why can the Moon exactly cover the Sun during a total solar eclipse?
options: The Sun is about 400 times wider and 400 times farther away
questions.explanation: By coincidence, the Sun is about 400 times larger than the Moon and about 400 times farther away, so they look the same size.
questions.funFact: This coincidence won't last, since the Moon is slowly moving away.

questions.question: How fast is the Moon drifting away from Earth each year?
questions.explanation: Measurements from mirrors left by Apollo astronauts show the Moon recedes about 3.8 cm per year.
questions.funFact: Days on Earth are slowly getting longer for the same reason.

questions.question: What is a day on Mars called?
questions.explanation: A Martian day is called a sol and lasts about 24 hours and 37 minutes.
questions.funFact: Mars rovers count missions in sols.

questions.question: Which galaxy's black hole was the first ever photographed, in 2019?
questions.explanation: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration released the first black hole image in April 2019, showing M87*'s shadow.
questions.funFact: A picture of our own galaxy's black hole, Sagittarius A*, followed in 2022.
